_comment: This repo's OWN declared ceilings for text a session loads before it
does any work. Repo-owned, never vendored: precedent_vendor_engine.py
lists this file as engine-READ but never engine-OWNED, so an engine
refresh will not overwrite the numbers below. They are mine to set.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL, 2026-09-11. The resident block is ONE
2000-token budget shared across every source a session resolves --
universal + team + individual combined -- and no practice SET can see
that total. precedent_resolve.py, which computes it, is in upstream's
CONSUMER_ENGINE_FILES and deliberately not in ENGINE_FILES: a set
resolves no catalogue, so it does not vendor the resolver. Each set
therefore measured only its own share, reported a healthy number, and
passed -- while the combined block sat at ~2047 tokens and overflowed.
Every local check was green the whole time.
resident_block_tokens below is this set's ALLOCATION of that shared
2000, not a private budget. It converts a global constraint nobody can
see into a local one build_views.py already enforces: it reads this key
in place of its 2000 literal and exits non-zero when the block exceeds
it. As long as every source's allocation sums to <= 2000, local green
implies global green -- which is the only way a set can police a budget
it cannot measure.
THE ALLOCATION, and the arithmetic behind it. After the 2026-09-11
demotions the combined block is ~1696 tokens across 15 resident
practices: this set ~351 (2 practices), precedent-individual ~468
(3), and ~877 across the remaining 10 from the universal source
and the other team sets. Allocations were set at roughly current + 18%
headroom, evenly applied:
precedent-individual           550   (currently ~468)
precedent-team-working-style   425   (currently ~351)
everything else, implied      1025   (currently ~877)
THE IMPLIED 1025 IS NOT DECLARED ANYWHERE, and that is this mechanism's
weak point, stated rather than hidden. Only the two sets above carry a
file like this one; the universal source and the other team sets keep
the 2000 default, so nothing stops their sum drifting past 1025 and
nothing here would notice. Re-derive the split whenever a source is
added or a practice changes tier, and treat these numbers as a running
hand-maintained agreement, not a computed fact.
The real gate remains very_deep_check.py's SESSION LOAD section, which
sums every attached source -- precedent_check.py's own session-load-budget
check says so in as many words -- but it runs only from a BestPractice
checkout with read access to these private sets. Until that runs on a
schedule, this file is the cheap approximation of it.
surfaces below is the SECOND, different budget: whole always-loaded
FILES rather than the resident block inside one. AGENTS.md and
CLAUDE.md were the only surfaces this repo had until 2026-09-22 (this
was written 'no .precedent/ here', citing the session-start-hook ->
additionalContext channel note in spec/PACK_SESSION_DOES_NOT_LOAD_
UNIVERSAL.md in BestPractice -- true when written, on 2026-09-11, and
false from the moment the vendor-refresh-followup PR (#61/#62) added
the universal-catalogue hook and the CLAUDE.md stub here: this set now
renders and injects .precedent/SESSION_PRACTICES.md into every session
the same as precedent-individual does, and that surface sat undeclared
for two merges before anyone measured it -- see its own entry below.
IT USED TO BE DECLARED BUT NOT CHECKED, and that has also changed.
This paragraph said precedent_check.py's session-load-budget check
reports SKIPPED here because there is no practices/session-load-
budget.md -- true against the engine version this file was written
against, and wrong since BestPractice PR #553 (2026-09-22): the check
now binds on tools/session_load_budgets.json existing (check()'s
binds_when), not on vendoring the practice text, precisely because a
repo that writes a ceiling down has opted in whether or not it carries
the prose that explains it. `python3 tools/precedent_check.py --full-
sweep` in this repo now actually reads every entry below and reports a
real VIOLATION for one that is missing, which is how the gap below was
found rather than merely suspected.
resident_block_tokens above is the half that DOES bite here, and it was
verified rather than assumed: set temporarily to 300 against a ~351
block, build_views.py exits 1 with "over the 300-token hard cap".
_headroom_comment: Read by tools/session_load_trend.py's headroom_notice(), called from
tools/precedent_gate.py's merge and push gates -- a NOTICE, never a
failure, that fires once a surface's headroom falls at or under this
percent of its ceiling. Was ABSENT here until 2026-09-22, the same gap
that let precedent-individual's AGENTS.md cross its ceiling with zero
warning that day (BestPractice's own precedent_check.py, PR #553, now
flags a source set that declares surfaces/ceilings but no floor).
5, matching BestPractice's own value -- see its
tools/session_load_budgets.json for the arithmetic behind that number.

AGENTS.md._note: ~832 tokens on 2026-09-11. Ceiling is current + ~20%. Most of the file is the generated loader block; the hand-written half is the repo notes above and below it.

CLAUDE.md._note: 111 tokens on 2026-09-20, the day the file was added -- the Claude Code adapter stub (@AGENTS.md include plus its explanatory comment), from templates/harness/claude-code/CLAUDE.md in BestPractice. Ceiling matches BestPractice's own CLAUDE.md surface entry, used as the model here.

.precedent/SESSION_PRACTICES.md._note: 5,773 tokens measured 2026-09-22 (tools/build_views.py's _approx_tokens against the file on disk, the same function precedent_check.py's session-load-budget check uses). Ceiling is measured + ~16%, the same headroom precedent-individual used when it declared this surface's entry on 2026-09-13. This is the surface flagged by a bare `python3 tools/precedent_check.py --full-sweep` in this repo: the vendor-refresh-followup PR (#61/#62) turned on the hook that renders and injects this file every session, and nobody added the ceiling that pairs with turning that hook on -- the same install step precedent-individual got on 2026-09-13 together with its own hook. Declaring it now closes that gap; it does not undo it, since the surface has been genuinely loaded, unmeasured, since the hook went live. Untracked and rebuilt at every session start from whatever universal and shared sources resolve, so it varies -- rerun the measurement and ratchet the ceiling down on a real reduction, never raise it to make a red check green.
